title: Cerebral bases of subliminal speech priming
function: Direct evidence that lexical processing can occur without reportable word identification.
finding: Masked, compressed spoken words influenced subsequent word processing. Repetition-related responses in temporal and insular regions occurred with prime identification near chance.
scope: Short, tightly controlled primes; repetition suppression indexes altered processing, not a measured emotional or therapeutic response.

title: Subliminal speech priming
design: Controlled experiments with compressed and masked speech
function: Establishes a behavioural route from a masked acoustic signal to word-level representations.
finding: Masked speech produced repetition priming, including effects across different voices. Evidence for semantic overlap was more limited.
scope: Word identity, phonological processing and sentence meaning are distinct levels of processing.

title: The effects of speech masking on neural tracking of acoustic and semantic features of natural speech
design: EEG during stories presented with competing speech
function: Shows how speech meaning and timing can remain represented when competing sound obscures speech.
finding: Acoustic and semantic tracking changed differently with masking. Semantic tracking remained measurable across several masking levels and weakened under the most severe masking.
scope: Participants attended to the stories; partially intelligible speech is distinct from objectively undetectable speech.

title: Perceptual restoration of masked speech in human cortex
function: Demonstrates reconstruction of missing speech information using surviving acoustic cues and expectations.
finding: Neural responses reflected the speech sounds listeners perceived when noise replaced parts of words. Context and prior neural activity helped explain restoration.
scope: The experiment replaced parts of speech; it did not remove all acoustic information from an entire message.

title: Enhanced neural speech tracking through noise indicates stochastic resonance in humans
design: Five EEG experiments; peer-reviewed version of record
function: Identifies a testable mechanism through which some noise conditions enhance early speech tracking.
finding: Minimal background noise enhanced neural tracking of speech amplitude onsets across a series of experiments.
scope: Speech remained intelligible and louder than the added noise. The result depends on signal-to-noise conditions and does not establish a universal mixing level.

title: Auditory neural tracking and lexical processing of speech in noise: Masker type, spatial location, and language experience
journal: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
function: Explains why masking, listening conditions and learned language knowledge alter speech extraction.
finding: Masker type, spatial separation and language experience influenced neural tracking and lexical processing of attended speech.
scope: The task involved attended sentences; it does not establish full comprehension at every masking level.

title: Neural Correlates of Auditory Perceptual Awareness under Informational Masking
design: MEG; detected and undetected tones in competing sounds
function: Separates sensory encoding from conscious access, a foundation for studying masked-language processing.
finding: Early auditory responses persisted for undetected tones, while later activity tracked perceptual awareness.
scope: Tone detection establishes an auditory processing principle; linguistic decoding requires additional evidence.

title: Neural markers of speech processing during inattentional deafness
function: Supports lexical processing outside focal attention and motivates tests during music listening.
finding: Neural differences between words and pseudowords remained measurable when attention was occupied and participants failed to notice the speech.
scope: Inattention and acoustic masking are different routes to reduced awareness. Task relevance affected processing.

title: Neurophysiological Evidence for Semantic Processing of Irrelevant Speech and Own-Name Detection in a Virtual Café
design: EEG and skin conductance; 50 recruited participants
function: Connects unattended language, personal relevance and physiological measures.
finding: Unattended café speech elicited responses related to semantic violations and personally significant own-name information.
scope: Irrelevant speech was audible; own-name effects do not establish an effect for every familiar phrase.

title: Exposure to subliminal arousing stimuli induces robust activation in the amygdala, hippocampus, anterior cingulate, insular cortex and primary visual cortex: a systematic meta-analysis of fMRI studies
function: Provides a general bridge between reduced awareness and emotion-related neural responses.
finding: Subliminal emotional stimuli recruited networks involved in salience and emotion; evidence differed by stimulus type, with prominent facial-stimulus findings.
scope: Much of this literature is visual. Its contribution is a cross-modal hypothesis about emotional processing.

title: Task-induced attention load guides and gates unconscious semantic interference
function: Helps formulate when limited attention may permit or constrain implicit meaning processing.
finding: Attentional load modulated unconscious semantic interference.
scope: Visual-word experiments; transfer to auditory music masking remains a research question.

title: The effect of speech masking on the human subcortical response to continuous speech
design: Auditory brainstem responses to competing speech; 25 participants
function: Extends the evidence map to early auditory encoding and signal degradation.
finding: Brainstem responses to individual speech streams remained measurable in mixtures. More competing talkers reduced response amplitude and increased latency.
scope: Published in 2025 after the indexed preprint. Brainstem encoding is an early processing stage, distinct from understanding meaning.

title: Effect of therapeutic suggestions during general anaesthesia on postoperative pain and opioid use: multicentre randomised controlled trial
design: Multicentre double-blind randomized controlled trial; 385 analysed
function: High-quality clinical evidence that externally delivered audio during an unconscious state may influence later physiological or behavioural outcomes.
finding: Music with therapeutic suggestions during general anaesthesia reduced postoperative opioid use relative to a blank recording. Median morphine-equivalent use was 4.0 versus 5.3 mg.
scope: The intervention combined music and suggestions. Anaesthesia differs from awake masking, and the design does not isolate the spoken component.

title: Efficacy of therapeutic suggestions under general anesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis; 32 randomized trials, 2,102 patients
function: Places anaesthesia audio studies in a larger evidence base and identifies outcomes with stronger or weaker signals.
finding: Pooled results found small effects for medication use and recovery, with little or no overall effect for pain and distress.
scope: Trials varied in interventions and methods. A review of trials is not itself a double-blind trial.

title: Plasticity and language in the anaesthetized human hippocampus
design: Human hippocampal single-unit recordings during anaesthesia
quality: Direct human neuronal recordings; small sample
function: Adds direct human neuronal evidence that language-related processing can persist during an unconscious state.
finding: Hippocampal recordings during propofol anaesthesia showed responses to language features and learning-related patterns. Natural-speech analyses included four participants and 375 units.
scope: Small neurosurgical sample; intact speech under anaesthesia is distinct from speech masked beneath music.

title: Double-Blind Tests of Subliminal Self-Help Audiotapes
design: Double-blind randomized experiments; 237 participants across three replications
function: A strong design reference for separating message effects, expectations and general listening effects.
finding: A month of use produced no content-specific improvement in the targeted memory or self-esteem measures. Perceived improvement followed tape labels.
scope: These null outcomes constrain those tested self-help recordings; they do not negate auditory encoding or word priming.

title: Effect of Subliminal Auditory Stimulation on Components of Auditory Late Responses and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data in Adults with Normal Hearing
design: Small controlled exposure study; EEG and fMRI
function: A close delivery match for testing whether repeated speech beneath music can alter subsequent neural responses.
finding: Words masked beneath instrumental music were presented repeatedly over ten days. The study reported changes in auditory evoked-potential amplitudes and some fMRI responses.
scope: Small groups and incompletely clear allocation and participant flow. Responses to audible test words were measured after exposure; structural brain change and emotional benefit were not established.

title: Positive effects of subliminal stimulation on memory
function: An early positive behavioural signal linking masked verbal stimulation with memory performance.
finding: The subliminal music group improved name recall after a short exposure; silence and music comparison groups were also included.
scope: The abstract reports within-group improvement; a verified between-group effect and blinding details are needed for stronger inference.

title: Is there an effect of subliminal messages in music on choice behavior?
journal: Journal of Articles in Support of the Null Hypothesis
design: Participant-blinded controlled experiments; 66 adults and 82 children
function: Tests a specific step from masked messages to overt decisions and helps select sensitive endpoints.
finding: Messages embedded in music did not reliably change the tested word or drink choices.
scope: Choice outcomes differ from neural encoding, autonomic response and longer-term learning.

title: Psychophysiological responses to subliminal auditory suggestions for activation
function: An early physiological link for testing autonomic responses to masked verbal content.
finding: Masked activating suggestions were associated with a heart-rate response during a stress task; skin conductance did not show the same effect.
scope: Small, older study; heart rate is not heart-rate variability and the measures are not interchangeable.

title: Subliminal Priming with Positive Auditory Stimuli Significantly Improves Self-Esteem and Emotional Well-Being
journal: European Journal of Medical and Health Sciences
design: Retrospective service study; 535 adults and children
function: Provides an observational signal and candidate psychological outcomes for prospective controlled work.
finding: Self-reported wellbeing improved during a programme of repeated positive auditory sessions.
scope: No randomized comparator; provider involvement and self-report limit causal attribution. The publication title is retained verbatim.

title: Effectiveness of subliminal audio messages on depression and anxiety in women with hypertension: a quasi-experimental study
function: Adds a preliminary clinical signal and a population for further replication.
finding: The report describes reduced anxiety and depression after six weeks of subliminal-audio sessions.
scope: Purposive recruitment; allocation, blinding and comparator details require full methodological confirmation. No verified double-blind classification.

title: Positive Auditory Stimuli and Its Effects on PTSD: A Case Study on Police Officers
journal: European Journal of Medical and Health Sciences
function: Descriptive material for generating outcome questions and documenting intervention delivery.
finding: The report describes self-reported changes during a positive-auditory-stimulation programme.
scope: Three uncontrolled cases, provider involvement and subjective outcomes; no causal estimate.

title: Subliminal Priming Effects on Motor and Cognitive Performance: Pilot Evidence With Implications for Neurorehabilitation
design: Single-blind randomized pilot; 30 participants, three priming modalities
function: Extends the outcome map beyond self-report and suggests objective performance measures.
finding: The pilot compared priming modalities and reported selective motor and cognitive findings.
scope: Small groups, multiple outcomes and no sham group; selective findings need replication.

title: The neurophysiological correlates of religious chanting
design: EEG and ECG in experienced practitioners; supplementary single-person fMRI
function: Helps frame the role of learned meaning, practice and personally meaningful mantra associations.
finding: Silent internal religious chanting was associated with neural and cardiac differences across comparison conditions.
scope: Participants actively recited internally. This is silent mental mantra, a different intervention from an external masked recording.

title: Repetitive Religious Chanting Modulates the Late-Stage Brain Response to Fear- and Stress-Provoking Pictures
design: EEG; active chanting and emotional pictures
function: Supports testing whether learned associations and repetition alter later emotional appraisal.
finding: Religious chanting modulated later brain responses to negative pictures.
scope: Active chanting; overlap with related research samples may limit independence. Early and late responses differed.

title: Effect of rosary prayer and yoga mantras on autonomic cardiovascular rhythms: comparative study
function: Identifies respiration as an important pathway and measurement variable in mantra-related autonomic effects.
finding: Recitation slowed breathing towards six breaths per minute and increased cardiovascular rhythm coordination and baroreflex sensitivity.
scope: Active recitation directly changes breathing. An external masked track may not reproduce this respiratory behaviour.

title: Yogic meditation reverses NF-κB and IRF-related transcriptome dynamics in leukocytes of family dementia caregivers in a randomized controlled trial
design: Randomized active-meditation versus music study; 45 randomized, 39 completed
function: Provides a molecular endpoint precedent for a future controlled study of stress regulation.
finding: Eight weeks of Kirtan Kriya were associated with differences in leukocyte gene-expression patterns and inferred transcription-factor activity.
scope: Active multicomponent meditation, not masked audio. Peripheral gene expression does not establish a masked-language mechanism. Linked to the Lavretsky caregiver trial.

title: A pilot study of yogic meditation for family dementia caregivers with depressive symptoms: effects on mental health, cognition, and telomerase activity
function: Provides a precedent for combining psychological and cellular measurements.
finding: The active-meditation comparison assessed mood, cognition and telomerase activity after eight weeks.
scope: Related to the Black transcriptome report; these publications do not count as independent trials.

title: Digital meditation at scale: a randomized citizen science trial comparing four meditation practices
design: Randomized digital trial; 1,211 participants assigned to meditation or music conditions
function: A useful design and feasibility reference for digital delivery, active controls, HRV and EEG.
finding: Four weeks of practice were assessed with subjective, EEG and HRV measures. The preregistered primary findings did not survive multiplicity correction.
scope: Active practices, including mantra, differ from masked playback; substantial attrition complicates interpretation.

title: Music structure determines heart rate variability of singers
function: Shows why respiration and musical structure need measurement alongside any spoken-message manipulation.
finding: Musical phrasing and breathing patterns organised heart-rate variability during singing and mantra-like phrases.
scope: Active vocalisation and coordinated breathing; this mechanism is not automatically present during passive masked listening.

title: Cardiovascular and nervous system changes during meditation
function: Encourages endpoint-specific interpretation of autonomic effects.
finding: Cardiovascular and neural measures changed during meditation; HRV measures did not all move in the same direction.
scope: Different HRV indices reflect different processes and depend on respiration, timing and experience.

title: Beating stress: music with monaural beats reduces anxiety and improves mood in a non-clinical population
function: Documents potential effects from the carrier audio itself, informing controls for masked-language research.
finding: The trial compared music with monaural beats, beats and pure-tone conditions on anxiety and mood.
scope: No music-only arm; nonlinguistic beats are distinct from verbal messages.

title: Inducing unconscious stress: Cardiovascular activity in response to subliminal presentation of threatening and neutral words
function: Indexes a route for examining semantic content and autonomic measures across modalities.
finding: Threatening versus neutral masked words increased total peripheral resistance significantly. Mean arterial pressure and HRV followed the predicted directions without statistically significant differences.
scope: Visual presentation; the cardiovascular endpoints differed in statistical support. Transfer to auditory masking remains a research question.

title: What Is Meditation? Proposing an Empirically Derived Classification System
function: Helps separate internally repeated mantra from an external acoustic intervention.
finding: The paper maps different meditation practices and terminology.
scope: Terminology and classification context; not a test of masked-speech effects.

title: Do Subliminal Messages Work?
function: Retained for provenance and for tracing the background rationale to primary research.
finding: Explainer supplied in the original research discussion.
scope: Not a peer-reviewed experiment; empirical claims are evaluated through the linked primary-source index.

title: The science of auditory masking
function: Introduces terminology and preserves the original source trail.
finding: Overview of auditory masking supplied in the original discussion.
scope: Commercial background material; not an independent neural or clinical study.

title: Supplied video reference · BEBxeP-1fAU
function: Preserves the supplied reference without assigning unverified scientific findings.
finding: The original video link is retained for completeness.
scope: Title, authorship and substantive content were not verified; no evidence rating assigned.
